questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: Which four crystal types are listed at the start of the chapter?
opts: Monosodium urate monohydrate (MSUM), CPPD, basic calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite) and calcium oxalate
Cholesterol, cystine, bilirubin and protein crystals only
Uric acid, calcium carbonate, magnesium and phosphate
Drug crystals, immunoglobulin, lipid and mucin
questions.exp: Types: 1. monosodium urate monohydrate (msum); 2. calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD); 3. basic calcium phosphate (BCP) — calcium hydroxy apatite; 4. calcium oxalate. (Book p543)

questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: How is basic calcium phosphate specified chemically on this page?
questions.exp: BCP is written as calcium hydroxy apatite Ca5(PO4)3OH. (Book p543)

questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: Which pathogenesis label and pathway open the crystal arthropathy block?
opts: Autoinflammatory syndrome with activation of the inflammasomal pathway converting pro-IL1β to IL-1β
questions.exp: Pathogenesis: autoinflammatory syndrome; activation of inflammasomal pathway; inflammasomes are innate-immunity intracellular protein complexes containing caspases that convert Pro-IL1β to IL-1β. (Book p543)

questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: Which definition of inflammasomes is printed?
opts: Innate immunity intracellular protein complex containing caspases
questions.exp: Parenthetical note: inflammasomes — innate immunity, intracellular protein complex containing caspases. (Book p543)

questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: Which three presentations are listed for monosodium urate monohydrate disease?
opts: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia, renal manifestations and gouty arthritis
questions.exp: MSUM presentations: asymptomatic hyperuricemia, renal manifestations, gouty arthritis. (Book p543)

questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: What is the printed dietary/endogenous source of uric acid?
questions.exp: URIC ACID source: purines (adenine, guanine). (Book p543)

questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: Which enzyme converts hypoxanthine and xanthine toward uric acid in the printed pathway?
questions.exp: The metabolism diagram places xanthine oxidase on the hypoxanthine→xanthine→uric acid steps. (Book p543)

questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: What does the printed note about uricase state for humans?
opts: Allantoin is the main human end-product
Uricase converts uric acid to allantoin, which is not present in humans, so uric acid is not metabolised
questions.exp: Note: uric acid —uricase→ allantoin (not present in humans → uric acid not metabolised). (Book p543)

questions.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
questions.q: In the AMP arm of the printed pathway, which enzyme acts between adenosine and inosine?
questions.exp: AMP → adenosine —(adenosine deaminase)→ inosine → hypoxanthine → xanthine → uric acid. (Book p543)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: What uric-acid pool size and daily excretion splits are printed on the purine diagram?
opts: No defined pool with 3 g daily loss
Pool 1.2 g; intestine 0.2 g/day and kidney 0.5 g/day with overall excretion 0.7 g/day
Pool 5 g with renal excretion only 0.05 g
Pool 0.2 g with faecal loss 2 g
questions.exp: Diagram: uric acid pool 1.2 g; intestine (0.2 g/day); kidney (0.5 g/day); excretion (0.7 g/day). (Book p544)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: What excretion rate is labelled to produce uricosuria?
questions.exp: Excretion greater than 7 mg/kg/d → uricosuria. (Book p544)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: Which three stone-formation thresholds and components are tabulated?
opts: Uric acid over 3 only; calcium over 8; citrate over 20
Uric acid greater than 7 mg/kg/d (hyperuricosuria); calcium greater than 4 (hypercalciuria, most common); citrate less than 11 (hypocitraturia)
questions.exp: Important causes of stone formation: >7 uric acid — hyperuricosuria; >4 calcium — hypercalciuria (m/c); <11 citrate — hypocitraturia. (Book p544)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: Which component is most common for stone formation in the printed table?
questions.exp: The calcium row is annotated m/c for stone formation. (Book p544)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: What mnemonic numbers summarize the four-compartment model of renal uric-acid handling?
questions.exp: 4 compartment model: 100 / 50 / 40 / 10. (Book p544)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: What handling steps map to the four compartments?
opts: 100% filtered in glomerulus; 100% reabsorbed at S1; 50% secreted at S2; 40% reabsorbed at S3; 10% excreted in urine
questions.exp: Model: 100% filtered in glomerulus; 100% reabsorbed at S1; 50% secreted at S2; 40% reabsorbed at S3; 10% excreted in urine. (Book p544)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: What net reabsorption percentage of filtered uric acid is printed?
questions.exp: Net reabsorption of 90% of filtered uric acid. (Book p544)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: Where do uric acid and phosphorus metabolism take place according to the source?
opts: Only in the proximal convoluted tubule
Entirely in the loop of Henle
questions.exp: Uric acid and phosphorus metabolism takes place only in PCT. (Book p544)

questions.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
questions.q: How does fractional excretion of uric acid and phosphorus change in proximal versus distal RTA?
opts: Raised in proximal RTA; normal in distal RTA
Normal in proximal; raised in distal
questions.exp: Fractional excretion of uric acid and phosphorus: increased in proximal RTA; normal in distal RTA. (Book p544)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: How is hyperuricemia framed relative to metabolic syndrome in the source?
opts: Hyperuricemia is a part of metabolic syndrome
questions.exp: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: hyperuricemia is a part of metabolic syndrome. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: What sex-specific diagnostic levels are printed for hyperuricemia?
opts: Equal to 5 mg/dl for both sexes
Greater than 6 mg/dl in females and greater than 7 mg/dl in males
questions.exp: Levels: greater than 6 mg/dl in females, greater than 7 mg/dl in males. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: What pregnancy-age pathway to adult metabolic syndrome is diagrammed?
opts: Increasing maternal age → small-for-gestational-age babies → pre-eclampsia → decreased nephron number → adult metabolic syndrome
Younger age → macrosomia → no nephron effect
questions.exp: Age at pregnancy flow: ↑age → small for gestational age babies → pre-eclampsia → ↓nephron number → metabolic syndrome as adults. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: What is the majority genetic split printed for unidentified hyperuricemia causes?
questions.exp: Unidentified (majority): 90% under-excretion, 10% over-production of urate. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: Which syndrome results from HGPRTase deficiency with its printed features?
opts: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome with hyperuricemia, self-mutilation and mental retardation
von Gierke disease with hepatomegaly only
questions.exp: HGPRTase deficiency → Lesch Nyhan syndrome: hyperuricemia, self-mutilation, mental retardation. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: Which enzyme defect and clinical cluster define von Gierke disease on this page?
opts: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (glycogen storage disease type 1) with hepatomegaly, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia, doll facies, hypoglycemia and seizures
questions.exp: Glucose 6 phosphatase deficiency → von Gierke's disease / glycogen storage disease type 1 with hepatomegaly, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia, doll facies, hypoglycemia and seizures. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: Which two remaining genetic defects are listed without disease names in the table?
opts: Fructose-1-phosphate aldolase deficiency and PRPP synthase overactivity
questions.exp: Table rows: fructose 1 phosphate aldolase deficiency; phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (PRPP) synthase overactivity. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: Which drug list is encoded by the printed CANT LEAP mnemonic?
opts: Cyclosporine, alcohol, nicotine, thiazides, loop diuretics, ethambutol, low-dose aspirin and pyrazinamide
Penicillamine, amiodarone, nitrofurantoin, ketamine, loop blockers, estrogen, ACE inhibitors, prednisolone
questions.exp: Secondary drug-induced hyperuricemia mnemonic CANT LEAP: cyclosporine, alcohol, nicotine, thiazide diuretics, loop diuretics, ethambutol, aspirin low dose, pyrazinamide. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
questions.q: Prolonged asymptomatic hyperuricemia with recurrent flares evolves as the printed progression shows toward what end state?
opts: Isolated kidney stones only without arthritis
Chronic tophaceous gout after multiple acute episodes
questions.exp: Progression: prolonged asymptomatic hyperuricemia → increased risk of acute gout with multiple episodes → chronic tophaceous gout. (Book p545)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: What serum urate threshold is attributed to Kelley's textbook?
questions.exp: Note: greater than 6.8 mg/dl (Kelley's textbook). (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: Which listed factor does NOT belong among the printed modifiers of urate level?
opts: Diet of seafood and red meat plus serum creatinine
questions.exp: Factors affecting: age, blood pressure, alcohol, diet (sea food, red meat), Sr. creatinine — platelet count is not listed. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: When is serum urate said to rise in men and women, and what pregnancy state is noted?
opts: Men at puberty; women at menopause; pregnancy is a hyperuricemic state
Men at menopause; women at puberty; pregnancy is normouricemic
questions.exp: Sr. urate increases in men at puberty, women at menopause; pregnancy is a hyperuricemic state. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: Which three renal manifestations with pathogenesis are tabulated?
opts: Uric acid nephropathy (TLS precipitation → AKI); urate nephropathy (prolonged hyperuricemia → CTID → CKD); urolithiasis (excretion greater than 7 mg/kg/day → stones)
questions.exp: Renal manifestations table: uric acid nephropathy via TLS precipitation in tubules → AKI; urate nephropathy via chronic tubulo-interstitial disease → CKD; urolithiasis when excretion exceeds 7 mg/kg/day. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: Tumour lysis syndrome causes urate precipitation in tubules with acute kidney injury. Which renal label applies?
questions.exp: Uric acid nephropathy pathogenesis: tumour lysis syndrome → precipitation of uric acid in tubules → AKI. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: What sex and age pattern is printed for acute gouty arthritis?
opts: Male 80% greater than female (post-menopausal); age 40–60 years
questions.exp: Acute gouty arthritis: sex M (80%) greater than F (post-menopausal); age 40–60 yrs. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: Which trigger and historical label are printed for acute gout?
opts: Alcohol as most common trigger; disease of King due to presentation in King Henry
questions.exp: Trigger: alcohol (m/c); AKA disease of King (d/t presentation in King Henry). (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: What percentage of first attacks involves the first MTP joint, and what is uric-acid status in 40%?
opts: 85% first MTP; uric acid normal or low in 40%
questions.exp: First attack: 1st MTP joint (85%); uric acid normal or low in 40%. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: What percentage has polyarticular first attacks, and which associations are printed?
opts: 15% with myeloproliferative neoplasm and post-transplant association
questions.exp: 15% have polyarticular involvement, associated with myeloproliferative neoplasm and post transplantation. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: What duration and joint signs are printed for the first acute attack?
opts: 3–14 days with hot, red, dusky swollen joint and periarticular erythema; pain peaks 4–12 hours
questions.exp: Duration 3–14 days; signs hot, red, dusky, swollen joint plus periarticular erythema; max intensity of pain 4–12 hrs. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
questions.q: Which four stages appear in the printed staging table?
opts: High uric acid levels, acute gout, intercritical gout and chronic gout
Prodrome, flare, tophus and surgery only
questions.exp: Staging: 1. high uric acid levels; 2. acute gout; 3. intercritical gout; 4. chronic gout with frequent pain and tophi formation. (Book p546)

questions.sec: Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
questions.q: Which joints and course describe subsequent gout attacks?
opts: Ankle, knee or wrist involvement with a variable course
First MTP only every time with fixed course
questions.exp: Subsequent attacks: involvement of ankle / knee / wrist; variable course. (Book p547)

questions.sec: Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
questions.q: Which condition is listed with gout as having a symptom-free baseline?
questions.exp: Symptom-free baseline seen in gout and palindromic rheumatology. (Book p547)

questions.sec: Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
questions.q: Which pair is printed as causes of acute monoarticular arthritis?
questions.exp: Acute monoarticular arthritis seen in gout and septic arthritis. (Book p547)

questions.sec: Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
questions.q: What WBC counts separate crystal arthritis from septic arthritis in the printed table?
questions.exp: Cytology table: WBC crystal arthritis 10,000–50,000; septic arthritis greater than 50,000. (Book p547)

questions.sec: Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
questions.q: How do focus of infection, culture/gram stain and other features differ in the table?
opts: Crystal has immunosuppression; septic has crystals
Crystal: no focus, negative culture/gram stain, presence of crystals; septic: focus positive, culture positive, immunosuppression plus
questions.exp: Table rows: focus of infection − versus +; culture and gram stain negative versus positive; other features — presence of crystals versus immunosuppression +. (Book p547)

questions.sec: Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
questions.q: What crystal morphology and birefringence are printed for gout on polarized light?
opts: Rhomboid crystals with weak positive birefringence
Needle-shaped crystals with strong negative birefringence
questions.exp: Polarized light microscopy: needle shaped crystals with strong negative birefringence. (Book p547)

questions.sec: Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
questions.q: What orientation note is printed for gout crystals under polarizing microscopy?
opts: Needle-shaped crystals are kept parallel to the light ray
questions.exp: Note polarising light microscopy: needle-shaped crystals kept parallel to light ray. (Book p547)

questions.sec: Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
questions.q: Which first-line agents are printed for acute gout?
opts: Indomethacin 50 mg TDS, colchicine with its staged regimen, and intra-articular steroids
questions.exp: First line: NSAIDs indomethacin 50 mg TDS; colchicine; intra-articular steroids. (Book p548)

questions.sec: Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
questions.q: How does the printed colchicine regimen act and what schedule is given?
opts: Prevents neutrophil migration and chemotaxis; 1.2 mg stat → 0.6 mg after 1 hr → 0.6 mg BD × 1 week → 0.6 mg OD × 3–6 months
Blocks xanthine oxidase with single 5 mg dose
questions.exp: Colchicine: prevents neutrophil migration & chemotaxis; 1.2 mg stat → 0.6 mg after 1 hr → 0.6 mg BD × 1 week → 0.6 mg OD × 3–6 months. (Book p548)

questions.sec: Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
questions.q: Which second-line trio is printed for gout flares?
opts: Anakinra (anti IL-1), single-dose IM ACTH injection, and IV pegloticase (recombinant uricase)
questions.exp: Second line: anakinra anti IL-1; IM ACTH injection (single dose); IV pegloticase (recombinant uricase). (Book p548)

questions.sec: Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
questions.q: Which three items form the printed ACR criteria of gout?
opts: Acute monoarticular arthritis, hyperuricemia and dramatic response to colchicine
Only elevated ESR and RF positivity
Joint stiffness over one hour with malar rash
questions.exp: ACR criteria of gout: acute monoarticular arthritis; hyperuricemia; dramatic response to colchicine. (Book p548)

questions.sec: Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
questions.q: What relapse percentage and ongoing deposition note define the intercritical period?
opts: 60% second flare within a year with continued tophaceous deposition and erosion
questions.exp: Intercritical period: symptom-free period, classical feature of crystal arthropathy; 60% second flare within a year; continued deposition of tophaceous gout and erosion. (Book p548)

questions.sec: Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
questions.q: Which chronic-gout x-ray features are printed?
opts: Asymmetric punched-out lytic lesions with overhanging edges (martel/G sign), sclerotic rat-bite erosions and maintained joint space
questions.exp: Chronic gout x-ray: asymmetric, punched out lytic, overhanging edges — martel sign / G sign; sclerotic margins — rat bite erosions; joint space maintained. (Book p548)

questions.sec: Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
questions.q: Which three structures are labeled on the knee ultrasound image?
opts: Uric acid crystals, hypoechoic hyaline cartilage and femoral cortex
questions.exp: Ultrasound of knee labels uric acid crystals, hypoechoic hyaline cartilage and femoral cortex. (Book p548)

questions.sec: Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
questions.q: How are tophi defined on this page?
opts: Irregular asymmetric moderately discrete tumescence of fingers due to subcutaneous MSUM crystal deposition, painless, sometimes with acute-on-chronic surrounding inflammation
Symmetrical warm nodules that are always painful
questions.exp: Tophi: irregular asymmetric moderately discrete tumescence of fingers d/t s/c deposition of msum crystals; painless; acute on chronic — acute inflammation surrounding tophi. (Book p549)

questions.sec: Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
questions.q: Which tophus site is marked most common, and what other sites are listed?
opts: Olecranon most common; also prepatellar bursa, ulnar surface, Achilles surface, myocardium and heart valves
questions.exp: Sites: olecranon (m/c), prepatellar bursa, ulnar surface, Achilles surface, myocardium, heart valves. (Book p549)

questions.sec: Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
questions.q: Which xanthine-oxidase inhibitors and key toxicities are printed?
opts: Colchicine as a xanthine oxidase blocker
Febuxostat with cardiotoxicity; allopurinol 300 mg daily with HLA-B5801 hypersensitivity, hairfall, liver and renal disease
questions.exp: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors: febuxostat (s/e cardiotoxicity); allopurinol 300 mg daily (s/e hypersensitivity in HLA B58-01 susceptibility, hairfall, liver and renal disease). (Book p549)

questions.sec: Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
questions.q: What allopurinol daily dose and hypersensitivity gene are printed?
opts: No fixed dose and no HLA link
questions.exp: Allopurinol 300 mg daily; s/e hypersensitivity in HLA B58-01 susceptibility. (Book p549)

questions.sec: Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
questions.q: Which agents are listed as uricosurics that enhance uric-acid excretion?
opts: Probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, benzbromarone, losartan (noted ACE inhibitor) and lesinurad
questions.exp: Uricosuric agents: probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, benzbromarone, losartan (ACE inhibitor), lesinurad. (Book p549)

questions.sec: Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
questions.q: Which recombinant uricases are printed and where else are they used?
opts: Rasburicase and pegloticase, also used in acute gout and tumour lysis syndrome
questions.exp: Recombinant uricase: rasburicase, pegloticase — also used in acute gout and TLS. (Book p549)

questions.sec: Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
questions.q: What interval between first attack and chronic gout is printed, and what drives tophus rate?
opts: 12 years between first attack and chronic gout; tophus formation rate correlates with degree and duration of hyperuricemia
questions.exp: Features: 12 yrs between first attack and chronic gout; rate of tophus formation correlates with degree and duration of hyperuricemia. (Book p549)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: Which demographic, symptom and gene notes open the CPPD section?
opts: Children with inflammatory monoarthritis and ANKH normal
Elderly, often asymptomatic and non-inflammatory, gene ANKH
questions.exp: CPPD: age elderly; asymptomatic; non-inflammatory; gene ANKH. (Book p550)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: How is chondrocalcinosis defined as the first CPPD presentation?
opts: Asymptomatic calcification of articular cartilage, predominantly of the knee
Painful erosion of the hip only
questions.exp: 1. Chondrocalcinosis: asymptomatic; calcification of articular cartilage; predominantly knee. (Book p550)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: Acute monoarticular CPPD arthritis with bloody aspiration, no hematogenous focus and no response to antibiotics or colchicine shows rhomboid weak-positive crystals. Which diagnosis?
questions.exp: Acute monoarticular CPPD: bloody aspiration; no hematogenous source of foci; no response to antibiotics and colchicine; rhomboid crystals with weak positive birefringence; pseudo-gout. (Book p550)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: What morphology and birefringence are printed for CPPD crystals?
opts: Rhomboid crystals with weak positive birefringence
Needle crystals with strong negative birefringence
questions.exp: Rhomboid crystals with weak positive birefringence. (Book p550)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: How is the chronic inflammatory CPPD polyarthritis pattern described?
questions.exp: 3. Chronic inflammatory polyarthritis: waxing & waning progression; non-erosive; pseudo RA. (Book p550)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: What MCP/wrist pattern with hook-like osteophytes is printed, and which disease is linked?
opts: Second and third MCP with wrist hook-like osteophytes seen in hemochromatosis; pseudo-OA
First CMC only with no link
questions.exp: 4. Involvement of MCP (2nd, 3rd), wrist: hook like osteophytes (seen in hemochromatosis); pseudo-OA. (Book p550)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: Which late presentations round out the CPPD list?
opts: Pseudo-neuropathic disease like Charcot; spondyloarthritis with crowned dens syndrome (dens in atlas); septic arthritis usually knee with fever
questions.exp: 5. Pseudo neuropathic disease presents like Charcot's; 6. spondyloarthritis — crowned dens syndrome (dens in atlas); 7. septic arthritis (m/c knee): fever. (Book p550)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: Which condition is printed as a CPPD association rather than a non-association?
opts: Hypomagnesemia as seen in Gitelman syndrome
questions.exp: Associations: hyperparathyroidism; hypophosphatasia (d/d of rickets with ↓ alkaline phosphatase); hypomagnesemia (seen in Gitelman syndrome); hemochromatosis. (Book p550)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: What crystal class and optical property define basic calcium phosphate?
opts: CPPD crystals that are weakly positive
MSUM needles that are strongly negative
questions.exp: Basic calcium phosphate: deposition of calcium hydroxyapatite crystals; non-birefringent. (Book p551)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: Which three BCP presentations are printed?
opts: Chronic calcific periarthritis most common in supraspinatus tendon; Milwaukee shoulder with rotator-cuff arthropathy and glenohumeral destruction; calcinosis cutis
questions.exp: Presentations: chronic calcific periarthritis m/c supraspinatus tendon; Milwaukee shoulder — rotator cuff arthropathy + glenohumeral destruction; calcinosis cutis. (Book p551)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: Which diseases are listed under calcinosis cutis?
opts: CREST syndrome and juvenile dermatomyositis (lipodystrophy, myofascial involvement)
questions.exp: Calcinosis cutis seen in CREST syndrome and juvenile dermatomyositis (lipodystrophy, myofascial involvement). (Book p551)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: What shape and birefringence are printed for calcium oxalate crystals, and what type-system is given?
opts: Pyramidal envelope-shaped crystals with strong positive birefringence; primary in hyperoxaluria, secondary in CKD
questions.exp: Calcium oxalate: strong positive birefringence; pyramidal, envelope shaped crystals; primary — hyperoxaluria, secondary — CKD. (Book p551)

questions.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
questions.q: What treatment note is printed for hyperoxaluria?
questions.exp: Note: mx of hyperoxaluria → combined kidney & liver transplantation. (Book p551)

units.title: 1. Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
units.sec: Crystal types, inflammasome pathogenesis and uric-acid metabolism
units.guide:
Four crystal classes and the inflammasome→IL-1β axis open the chapter. MSUM presentations and the purine-to-uric-acid pathway with absent uricase follow in printed order.
AMP/GMP branches and xanthine oxidase positions are retained exactly.

units.title: 2. Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
units.sec: Purine pools, stone thresholds and the four-compartment renal model
units.guide:
Dietary and endogenous purines feed a 1.2 g uric-acid pool with intestinal and renal excretion. Stone risk thresholds and the 100/50/40/10 tubular model follow.
Net 90% reabsorption, PCT-only handling and FEUA in RTA close the unit.

units.title: 3. Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
units.sec: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia: thresholds, genetics and drug causes
units.guide:
Metabolic-syndrome link and sex-specific thresholds open the unit. Pregnancy-age nephron pathway and the genetic enzyme table with Lesch-Nyhan/von Gierke follow.
CANT LEAP drugs and progression to chronic tophaceous gout close the page.

units.title: 4. Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
units.sec: Hyperuricemia modifiers, renal manifestations and acute gouty arthritis
units.guide:
Kelley threshold and modifiable factors precede the three renal outcomes. Acute gout demographics, King Henry label, first-attack features and four-stage table follow.
Hot-red-dusky signs and 3–14-day duration are retained as printed.

units.title: 5. Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
units.sec: Subsequent attacks, synovial-fluid distinction and polarized-light proof
units.guide:
Ankle/knee/wrist subsequent attacks and symptom-free baseline notes lead investigations. Crystal versus septic synovial table with WBC cut-offs follows.
Needle-shaped strong negative birefringence parallel to the light ray closes the unit.

units.title: 6. Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
units.sec: Acute gout treatment, ACR criteria, intercritical course and chronic imaging
units.guide:
First-line indomethacin, colchicine regimen and intra-articular steroids lead. Second-line anakinra, ACTH and pegloticase plus ACR triad follow.
Intercritical 60% relapse, martel/rat-bite x-ray and knee ultrasound signs close the unit.

units.title: 7. Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
units.sec: Tophi, xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and uricases
units.guide:
Tophus morphology, acute-on-chronic flares and preferred sites open the unit. Febuxostat/allopurinol with HLA-B5801 hypersensitivity lead the hypouricemics.
Uricosuric list, recombinant uricases and 12-year natural history close Chapter 28's gout therapy.

units.title: 8. CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
units.sec: CPPD presentations, associations and the basic crystal remainder
units.guide:
Elderly ANKH-linked CPPD opens with chondrocalcinosis and pseudo-gout features. Pseudo-RA, hook osteophytes, crowned dens and association list follow.
BCP Milwaukee/CREST material and calcium-oxalate transplant note close Chapter 28.
